q: Translocation is the movement of dissolved substances through a plant.
e: True. Translocation is the movement of dissolved substances through a plant.

q: Water and dissolved salts from the soil travel downwards through the vessels of the xylem.
e: False. In general, water and dissolved salts from the soil travel upwards through the vessels of the xylem and food synthesized in the leaves passes downwards or upwards in the sieve tubes of the phloem.

q: Food synthesized in the leaves passes downwards or upwards in the sieve tubes of the phloem.
e: True. Food synthesized in the leaves passes downwards or upwards in the sieve tubes of the phloem.

q: Carbohydrates produced by leaves are transported out of the leaf in the form of sucrose to the stem.
e: True. Carbohydrates produced by leaves are transported out of the leaf in the form of sucrose to the stem.

q: Both upward and downward movement may take place at the same time in the phloem.
e: True. Both upward and downward movement may take place at the same time in the phloem.

q: The phloem tissue is a complex tissue consisting of sieve tube, companion cell, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibre.
e: True. The phloem tissue is a complex tissue consisting of sieve tube, companion cell, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibre.

q: All components of the phloem tissue are living cells including the phloem fibre.

q: Sieve tubes or sieve cells have no nucleus and companion cells possess nuclei and work together.

q: Sieve cells can manage translocation without nuclei because they are kept alive by the nucleated companion cells.
e: True. Sieve cells can manage translocation without nuclei because they are kept alive by the nucleated companion cells.

q: There are profuse cytoplasmic connections between sieve and companion cells.
